note: Alberta Parks recreation area on North Buck Lake, 14 km northeast of Boyle on Hwy 663 then 4 km north on an access road: one loop of sites on a point between two arms of the lake and a larger loop by the beach, with a boat launch, cook shelter, playground, bike trails and a sand hill. Birds nest along the shoreline; give them space. --Claude
summary: Confirmed 67 power sites (15/30-amp) at $38, season May 14 - Sep 8 (2026), reservable 90 days ahead, vault toilets, hand-pump water (bring drinking water). The stored note's 'mix of unserviced and powered' was wrong: every site is powered. Added count, max length 51 ft, pull-throughs, season; note rewritten. Lakeview confirmed; phone, website and seniors line flagged.
flags: WATERFRONT (stored lakeview - confirmed): the shop tags 14 sites 'Near Water' (01, 03, 05, 07, 10, 12, 13, 14, 19, 21, 22, 23 on the point; 25, 27 by the beach). On Esri imagery (0.9 m/px) the point loop (sites 1-23, about 54.6620,-112.5232) is ringed by a belt of trees/shrub and a marshy fringe: west-side pads are about 25-40 m from the water through that belt, the north end has the loop road on the outside, and one east spur (around sites 12-14) ends perhaps 15-25 m from the east arm with partial tree cover. The south loop (24-67) is behind the shore road and a tree belt 40-60 m from the water. No pad clearly has only open ground to the water; lakeview stands. Lead: the east spur at the point (sites 12-14) if a reviewer sees open ground there.

PHONE (stored empty): page 'Information: 780-675-8213' (the tear sheet's Athabasca Area Office); tear sheet 'North Buck Campground Booth Seasonal Phone: 780-689-2074'. Suggest the booth number with the area office as alternate. No facility operator named.

WEBSITE: stored first line is the park root; the campground page is https://www.albertaparks.ca/parks/north/north-buck-lake-pra/information-facilities/camping/north-buck-lake/ (answered 200); shop link answered 200.
SENIORS LINE: this page carries 'This campground qualifies for the camping fee discount for Alberta seniors.' (the only page of the ten in this batch that does).

PIN (stored 54.66020,-112.52248 = the directions point): at the booth/parking junction between the point loop (~80 m north) and the south loop (~300 m south-west); inside the campground area - no move.
SAND: the south loop's pads are open sandy ground among pines with a 'Sand Hill' on the map - developed loop with gravel/sand pads on park roads, not beach camping.
